title: Release cadence and canary planning for Hosted API + Model Catalog
creator: Asha Patel
description: Define a repeatable quarterly release cadence and an operational canary playbook for introducing new model variants into the Hosted API model catalog. This ticket captures the product-level decisions required to: (1) standardize a release window cadence (weekly canaries within a quarterly plan), (2) define canary percentages and duration for traffic shifts, (3) set automated monitoring/rollback thresholds tied to SLOs, and (4) outline gating criteria for model onboarding (compatibility, eval pass-rate, cost delta guardrails). The goal is to give engineering reliable knobs and clear product requirements so model rollouts are predictable, low-risk, and auditable.
acceptance_criteria: A documented cadence is published (weekly canary windows + quarterly major rollouts) in Confluence
Canary plan includes: initial 1% traffic for 2 hours -> 5% for 6 hours -> 20% for 24 hours -> 100% with manual approval
Monitoring thresholds defined and wired into Console alerts: p95 latency delta > 30% OR error-rate > 0.2% OR quality regressed by > 3% triggers rollback
Model onboarding checklist created: unit tests, inferencing perf bench, quantization verification, eval suite pass-rates >= baseline
Playbook includes rollback and postmortem steps and links to the runbook; runbook tested in a dry-run during cycle
Owners assigned for each step (PM, Eng on-call, SRE, Design for UX gating)

rollout_plan_summary: Weekly canary windows during low-traffic weekdays: start with 1% (2h), ramp to 5% (6h), then 20% (24h). If monitoring passes for 48 hours at >=20% we request manual approval to proceed to 100%. Shorter ramp allowed for low-risk model patches. Each canary run includes synthetic traffic job and subset of production requests for quality sampling.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Latency regressions for quantized variants. Mitigation: require perf bench and add p95 SLA guardrail before canary allowed.
Risk: Noisy signals during holiday traffic. Mitigation: block major canaries within known irregular traffic windows; use synthetic traffic to provide stable signal.
Risk: Cost blowup for heavy models. Mitigation: cost-delta guardrail (max +35%) enforced; finance must approve exceptions.
Risk: Incomplete rollback automation. Mitigation: ensure runbook includes manual rollback path and ENG to deliver automation by next cycle.
decisions: SLO-based automated rollback conditions finalized (p95 delta, error rate, quality eval delta)
Quantized models require an additional perf/accuracy verification step before canary
Canary windows will be scheduled in a shared calendar and become part of the quarterly roadmap cadence
